```{r}
# Bring in other variables from the original data frame
HH <-  data.table(read_dta("IDHR71FL.DTA"))
IR <-  data.table(read_dta("IDIR71FL.DTA"))
HH$hhid <- str_trim(HH$hhid)
IR$caseid <- str_trim(IR$caseid)

HH$v001<-HH$hv001
HH$v002<-HH$hv002
IR$wt<-IR$v005/1000000

HH <- HH %>% 
  mutate(cook.fuel = case_when(
    hv226 == 1 ~ "Electricity",
    hv226 == 2 ~ "LPG",
    hv226 == 3 ~ "Natural gas",
    hv226 == 5 ~ "Kerosene",
    hv226 == 8 ~ "Wood",
    hv226 == 95 ~ "No food cooked",
    TRUE ~ "Other"))

IR.merge <- IR %>% select(v001, v002, caseid, v501, v213, m15_1, m13_1, m14_1, s428aa_1, s428ab_1, s428ac_1, s428ad_1, s428ae_1, s428af_1, s428ag_1, s428ah_1, s428aa_2, s428ab_2, s428ac_2, s428ad_2, s428ae_2, s428af_2, s428ag_2, s428ah_2)
#dim(IR.merge) #49627     5
HH.merge <- HH %>% select(v001, v002, cook.fuel, hv237, hv237a, hv237b, hv237c, hv237d, hv237e, hv237f)
#dim(HH.merge) #47963     9
newmerge <-merge(IR.merge, HH.merge, by=c("v001", "v002"), all.x=T)
#dim(newmerge) #49627    12
```

Read in saved data
```{r}
dhs.seg.comb <- readRDS("10_dhs.seg.comb.rds")
```

```{r}
#drop the duplicate women records
dhs.seg.comb <- dhs.seg.comb %>%
  distinct(caseid, .keep_all = TRUE)
#dim(dhs.seg.comb) #49309   323
dhs.seg.comb$k3 <- factor(dhs.seg.comb$k3)
dhs.seg.comb.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=dhs.seg.comb)

#In the following cases, I will apply survey design weights after specific data manipulation (e.g., filter, mutate). The survey weight is applied when we want to make inferences about the entire population from the sample data, and it is used to adjust for the survey's sampling design, such as unequal probabilities of selection, nonresponse, and stratification.

#Note that after apply survey weight, we may see decimals in frequency table. In survey analysis, weights reflect the number of units in the population that each sample unit represents. The weights can be any positive number, but not necessarily an integer. 
```

## 1. Segment Distribution
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#Here duplicates rows have been removed, to avoid overrepresenting women with 2+ children.

#Survey design weights are applied. The survey weights are applied when we want to make inferences about the entire population from the sample data, and it is used to adjust for the survey's sampling design, such as unequal probabilities of selection, nonresponse, and stratification.

#Note that after apply survey weights, we may see decimals in frequency table. In survey analysis, weights reflect the number of units in the population that each sample unit represents. The weights can be any positive number, but not necessarily an integer. 
```

### 1.1. Distribution 
```{r}
seg.tab <- svytable(~k3, design = dhs.seg.comb.des)
seg.pie <- as.data.frame(seg.tab)

seg.pie <- seg.pie %>%
  mutate(percent = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0),
         type = ifelse(substr(k3, 1, 1) == "R", "Rural", "Urban"))%>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(k3)) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_freq = cumsum(Freq),
         midpoint = cumulative_freq - (Freq/2))

# Define the color palette
rural_palette <- c("#ffd9b2ff", "#f5b068ff", "#f18619ff")
urban_palette <- c("#e5f0feff", "#99c4ff", "#002d8f5f")
palette <- c("Rural" = "#f18619ff", "Urban" = "#002d8f5f")
seg_colors <- setNames(c(rural_palette, urban_palette), unique(dhs.seg.comb$k3))

ggplot(seg.pie, aes(x = factor(1), fill = k3)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(weight = Freq), width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") + 
  geom_text(aes(y = midpoint, label = paste0(round(percent, 1), "%")), color = "black", size = 3.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = seg_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Segment") +
  theme_void() +
  ggtitle("Segment Distribution")

seg.pie
```

### 1.2. Age by segment
```{r}
#the thick bar represents the median value
# Calculate the median age by segment (k3) using the survey package
median_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.5), na.rm = TRUE)
median_age <- median_age %>% rename(median_age = age.yrs)

# Calculate the first and third quartiles
q1_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.25), na.rm = TRUE)
q1_age <- q1_age %>%  rename(q1 = age.yrs)
q3_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
q3_age <- q3_age %>%  rename(q3 = age.yrs)
min_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.0), na.rm = TRUE)
min_age <- min_age %>% rename(min = age.yrs)
max_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(1.0), na.rm = TRUE)
max_age <- max_age %>% rename(max = age.yrs)

age_stats <- full_join(q1_age, q3_age, by = "k3")
age_stats <- full_join(age_stats, median_age, by = "k3")
age_stats <- full_join(age_stats, min_age, by = "k3")
age_stats <- full_join(age_stats, max_age, by = "k3")

age_stats <- age_stats %>% 
  select("k3", "min", "q1", "median_age", "q3", "max")

ggplot(age_stats, aes(x = k3, y = median_age)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(lower = q1, upper = q3, middle = median_age, ymin = min, ymax = max), stat = "identity", fill = "grey80", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(median_age, 1), y = median_age), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), vjust = -0.5, color = "black", size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = seg_colors) + 
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Age", title = "Age Distribution by Segment") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

age_stats
```

### 2.1. Measures used in clustering

#### 2.1.1. Heatmap (binary)
```{r}
seg.k3 <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  select(c(bin.var),k3)

#dim(seg.k3)
seg.k3 <- seg.k3 %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(bin.var), ~ifelse(. == 2, 1, 0), .names = "prop_{.col}")) %>%
  group_by(k3) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("prop_"), mean)) 
seg.k3 <- seg.k3 %>% 
  mutate(area = ifelse(k3 == "R1" | k3 == "R2" | k3 == "R3", "Rural", "Urban"))
#view(seg.k3)

#define var.labels
custom_labels <- c(
  "marr.cohab" = "With partner",
  "early.cohab.19" = "Early marriage or cohabitation",
  "media.sum.2plus" = "Use 2+ media sources",
  "num.under15.2plus" = "With 2+ children U15",
  "hh.kidwom.rat.2plus" = "Ratio of U5 to women >=2",
  "husb.ed.mtprim" = "Partner edu more than primary",
  "highestyearsedinHH.7plus" = "7+ years of edu for HH",
  "hh.watpur.appr" = "Use water purify method",
  "hh.toilet.flush" = "Use flush toilet",
  "med.distance" = "Distance is a big problem",
  "med.alone" = "Going alone is a big problem",
  "med.permis" = "Getting permision is a big problem",
  "disc.fp.yn" = "Discuss FP with someone",
  "insurance.cov.cat1" = "Coverged by EPM insurance",
  "hh.land" = "Own land for agriculture"
)

# Reshape dataframe for ggplot
df_long <- seg.k3 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("prop_"), names_to = "var.label", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(var.label = str_remove(var.label, "prop_"),
         label = ifelse(var.label %in% names(custom_labels), custom_labels[var.label], var.label),
         label_percent = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1))
df_long <- merge(df_long, var, by.x = "var.label", by.y = "f.var.name")

df_long$category <- gsub("Woman and her past experiences", "Woman and her\npast experiences", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Household relationships", "Household\nrelationships", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Household economics and living conditions", "HH econ &\nliving cond.", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Health mental models", "Health mental\nmodels", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Social support", "Social\nsupport", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Human and natural systems", "H&N\nsystem", df_long$category)

df_long$category <- factor(df_long$category,

# Plot
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = factor(k3), y = label, fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(category), cols = vars(area), scales = "free", space = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#313695", mid = "#FFFFBF", high = "#A50026", midpoint = 0.5, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "Proportion within cluster", x = '', y = '', fill = 'Proportion within\ncluster') +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 180, size = 5),
```


```{r, fig.height = 8, fig.width=20}
# Prepare data
dhs.seg.comb <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(slum1 = case_when(
    slum1 == 1 ~ "rural",
    slum1 == 2 ~ "urban non-slum",
    TRUE ~ "urban slum"))

custom_labels <- c(
  "ed.lev.cat1" = "Women's edu",
  "wd.ownincome.cat" = "Women's deicision on own income",
  "jd.hlth.cat" = "Joined decision on women's health",
  "work.seasonal" = "Women's work",
  "water.cat" = "Water source",
  "partner.working" = "Partner's work",
  "auto.contra" = "Autonomy on contraceptive",
  "vehic.index" = "Vehicle ownership",
  "slum1" = "Slum or not"
)

#table(dhs.seg.comb$slum1)

long_dt <- dhs.seg.comb.cat %>%
  select(c(cat.var, 'k3')) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(cat.var), names_to = "variable", values_to = "level")

cluster_size <- long_dt %>%
  group_by(k3, variable) %>%
  summarize(cluster_total = n(), .groups = 'drop')

agg_dt <- long_dt %>%
  group_by(k3, variable, level) %>%
  summarize(ct = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
  left_join(cluster_size, by = c("k3", "variable")) %>% 
  mutate(pct = round((ct/cluster_total)*100, 2)) %>% 
  mutate(var.label = ifelse(variable %in% names(custom_labels), 
                            custom_labels[variable], 
                            variable))

agg_dt <- merge(agg_dt, var, by.x = "variable", by.y = "f.var.name")

agg_dt$category <- factor(agg_dt$category,

agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Women's edu", "Women's edu", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Women's deicision on own income", "Women's deicision\non own income", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Joined decision on women's health", "Joined decision\non women's health", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Women's work", "Women's work", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Water source", "Water source", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Partner's work", "Partner's work", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Autonomy on contraceptive", "Autonomy on\ncontraceptive", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Vehicle ownership", "Vehicle\nownership", agg_dt$var.label)

#view(agg_dt)
agg_dt <- agg_dt %>% 
  mutate(area = ifelse(k3 == "R1" | k3 == "R2" | k3 == "R3", "Rural", "Urban"))

# Define a manual color palette
my_colors <- c("0" = "#f9c696", "1" = "#FDB863" , "2" = "#BF5B17", "Full or partial autonomy" = "#ECEC26", "No control over" = "#FFFF99", "Not partnered" = "#F0027F", "Higher education" = "#386CB0", "Some eduction" = "#9cc2f4", "No eduction" = "#666666", "Not in union" = "#F0027F", "Not paid in cash or not working" = "#e0dcdc", "No" = "#666666","Yes" = "#D32F2F", "Not protected" = "#666666", "Open protected" = "#C7E9C0",  "Piped or borehole" = "#7FC97F", "Tank or packed" = "#259d25", "All  year" = "#563880", "Seasonal" = "#BEAED4", "Occassional" = "#e6dff1", "No work in the past 12 months" = "#666666", "Worked last 12 months" = "#8E24AA", "Worked last 7 days" = "#b590bf", "Not working or no partner"="#F0027F","rural" = "#ffd9b2ff", "urban non-slum" = "#f2a273f5", "urban slum" = "#d46f32f5")

# Plot
```

### 2.2. Variable breakdown: those in typing tool
```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Although wealth.index.ur.ord was found to be among the most influential in making splits in the tree (typing tool), it is difficult to use practically because this variable is from already-constructed DHS data. For instance, in the typing tool, it is difficult to ask questions to define what is wealth.index.ur.ord >= 3 or < 3.
# Referring to the method and procedures DHS followed to constructed wealth.index, I explored variables that contributed to wealth.index and after a few rounds of exploration, the results suggests use cooking.fuel together with toilet and vehicle ownership as the "alternative" of wealth.index. Note that toilet and vehicle ownership were already used as they were part of the differentiating variables. cook.fuel is the only variable that was not used in LCA modeling for clustering but used in typing tool.

# In the final trees (typing tool) we choose, we have:
  ##Urban: 12 variables actually used in tree construction: early.cohab.19, ed.lev.cat1, hh.toilet.flush, hh.watpur.appr, highestyearsedinHH.7plus, husb.ed.mtprim, insurance.cov.cat1, marr.cohab, media.sum.2plus, slum.sum, vehic.index, water.cat. 
  ##Rural: 12 variables actually used in tree construction: cook.fuel, ed.lev.cat1, hh.land, hh.toilet.flush,   hh.watpur.appr, highestyearsedinHH.7plus, husb.ed.mtprim, insurance.cov.cat1, marr.cohab, media.sum.2plus, vehic.index, water.cat (same 12 variables as urban, but they show up at differnet nods on the trees)      
```

#### 2.2.1. Relationship status
```{r}
#dhs.seg.comb$v501
seg.reship <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(status = case_when(
    v501 == 0 ~ "Never in union",
    (v501 == 1 | v501 == 2) ~ "Living w/ husband or partner",
    v501 == 3 ~ "Widowed",
    v501 == 4. ~ "Divorced",
    TRUE ~ "Separated"))

seg.reship.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=seg.reship)
seg.reship <- svytable(~k3 + status, design = seg.reship.des)
seg.reship <- as.data.frame(seg.reship)

seg.reship <- seg.reship %>% 
  group_by(k3) %>%
  mutate(perc = round((Freq/sum(Freq))*100, digits = 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

##recorder
seg.reship$status <- factor(seg.reship$status , levels = c("Living w/ husband or partner", "Never in union", "Widowed", "Divorced", "Separated"),labels = c("Living w/ husband or partner", "Never in union", "Widowed", "Divorced", "Separated"))

ggplot(seg.reship, aes(x = k3, y = perc, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(perc, "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Percentage", fill = "Relationship", title = "Distribution of Women by Relationship within Segment") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#9cc2f4", "#b4adaa", "#386CB0", "#03859b", "#b590bf", "#8E24AA", "#bf281c")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1))
  

seg.reship
```

#### 2.2.2. Women's education
```{r}
#table(dhs.seg.comb$ed.lev) #None (==0), incomplete primary (==1), complete primary (==2), incomplete secondary (==3), complete secondary (==4), higher education (==5)
seg.edu <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(ed.lev = case_when(
    ed.lev == 0 ~ "No education",
    ed.lev == 1 ~ "Incomplete primary",
    ed.lev == 2 ~ "Complete primary",
    ed.lev == 3 ~ "Incomplete secondary",
    ed.lev == 4 ~ "Complete secondary",
    ed.lev == 5 ~ "Higher education")) %>% 
  mutate(ed.lev = factor(ed.lev, levels = c("Higher education", "Complete secondary", "Incomplete secondary", "Complete primary", "Incomplete primary", "No education")))  

#sum(896,3792,8382,14105,13066,9068)
seg.edu.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=seg.edu)
seg.edu <- svytable(~k3 + ed.lev, design = seg.edu.des)
seg.edu <- as.data.frame(seg.edu)

seg.edu <- seg.edu %>% 
  group_by(k3) %>%
  mutate(perc = round((Freq/sum(Freq))*100, digits = 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(seg.edu, aes(x = k3, y = perc, fill = ed.lev)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(perc, "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Percentage", fill = "Educational Level", title = "Distribution of Women by Educational Level within Segment") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8E24AA","#b590bf","#03859b","#386CB0","#9cc2f4","#b4adaa")) +
```
